thread_title: S. leucophylla Hurricane Creek White clone E
breadcrumb: S. leucophylla Hurricane Creek White clone E

posts.body_html:
Just like the other clones, this one is also mysterious! The shape varies, and sometimes, the spring pitchers produce pink pigments.

All pictures below are S. leucophylla Hurricane Creek White clone E from Baldwin Co, AL-these are extinct in the wild:

Check out the pink coloration in this trap-there is a slight dent too-that was my bad...accidently bent the trap while it was developing. Perhaps that's what caused the serious pigments to occur:


Another shot:



And here is another division of clone E-almost looks like a completely different plant!!. In addition, there's a lot more green veins in the upper portion of the hood compared to the previous picture, and I'm starting to think these various phenotypes are highly environmentally induced. Some were divided last year, others weren't, which we all know affects the color of the plant.
And yes, they are 100% for sure the same clone:








Now here's the same exact clone, but in a different pot. Notice how the shape is slightly different.

posts.body_html: What a beautiful, impressive plant! I take it that that's a spring pitcher, the one that's close to a meter in height. Are the autumn pitchers generally taller, as is typical with leucophylla, and what colour is the flower?

posts.body_html:
Thanks Calen! Yes, don't be alarmed, all hurricane creek white plants, including the brighest white ones, can turn red under certain environmental conditions.

Kimbruun, yes, these are all spring pitchers, and the fall pitchers typically have brighter white colors. I also had very tall fall pitchers on Clone A, but clone E is the tallest. I think on the last photo, there are some flowers, but they're almost bloomed out. The petals on hurricane creek white are bright red, and they seem to be slightly brigher red in color when compared to other regular leucophyllas.

posts.body_html: Doh! You're right, meizzwang - I hadn't noticed the flower in that last shot. I seem to recall reading somewhere that there may be some introgression going on in some the Hurricane Creek leucophyllas, hence my interest in the colour of the flower. Which is in itself does not detract, but is merely a point of interest - the beauty of the plant speaks for itself, after all.

posts.body_html:
S. leucophylla Hurricane creek white clone E produced some monster traps again this year, and some of the traps are pretty darn white too! Other clones have equally ginormous rhizomes yet they don't quite get as big. The exception is clone F, which I haven't really allowed to get too big since everyone in the world wants a piece of it....I suspect clone F can get just as giant.

Anyhow, here's some more clone E pix, photos taken 9/7/15:






I really wish you could tell how big these traps are:
